subject: MSA + Order Form — exposure allocation and proposed liability model
messages:
From: Jane Morris <jane.morris@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbus-analytics.com
Date: 2026-12-05T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: MSA redlines — liability cap and exclusions

Olga,

Thanks for sending the initial MSA and order form. Our legal team reviewed and has two principal asks on limitation of liability: 1) a single aggregate cap rather than annualized buckets, and 2) carveouts for IP indemnity and willful misconduct only — we need consequential damages excluded broadly.

Specific redline in the attached MSA: limit Redwood's liability to the greater of $500,000 or the fees paid in the preceding 12 months (aggregate for the term). They flagged that a multiple-based cap (e.g., 3x monthly fees) would be unpredictable for budgeting.

We also requested an explicit cyber/data-breach carveout with a $1.5M cap in recognition of the sensitivity of the data we may send to hosted endpoints. Please confirm if Redwood can accept the aggregate approach or propose alternatives.

Best,
Jane Morris
Head of Legal
Nimbus Analytics

Attachment: Nimbus_MSA_Redline_v3.docx (MS Word redline of MSA)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jane Morris <jane.morris@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-06T09:24:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — liability cap and exclusions

Jane — thanks for the clear read. Looping in our legal lead Karthik and Markus on commercial impact. A few quick items up front:

- Redwood's standard position historically is a "greater of $X or N x monthly fees (annualized)" because it balances predictable minimum protection with a dollar cap tied to spend.
- We do accept carveouts for IP indemnity and fraud/willful misconduct; the data breach carveout is something we typically handle as a separate quantifiable exposure (we've seen customers want it higher for regulated data).

Karthik/Markus — can you suggest language that bridges the two approaches (aggregate vs annualized)? Also: Jane asked for consequential damages excluded broadly; that is standard and we can accept with the usual IP/data/indemnity carveouts.

Thanks — can we aim to have a short call Wednesday to finalize?

—Olga
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: OrderForm_Draft.pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-06T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: MSA redlines — liability cap and exclusions

Quick proposal for negotiation draft (high level):

1) Cap model: "Supplier's aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of (i) USD 250,000, or (ii) twelve (12) times the average monthly fees paid by Customer in the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the claim." This provides a floor while tying upside to spend.

2) Annualized vs aggregate: We can accept aggregate for the contract term rather than calendar-year aggregation, but request mutuality and per-incident sub-cap for certain classes (e.g., IP indemnity) so exposure isn't infinite.

3) Data/cyber carveout: Accept carveout for data breach but propose a separate, limited cap of USD 1,000,000 (we can make this higher under an enterprise addendum or through insurance proof).

4) Consequential damages: standard exclusion language.

If Nimbus insists on the higher $500k floor, we can trade towards a shorter termination right (e.g., 30-day notice for material breaches) or commit to SOC2 + annual pen-test report as comfort.

I suggest we share this text for an in-line redline and offer a 30-minute commercial call.

—Karthik
Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jane Morris <jane.morris@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-07T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — liability cap and exclusions

Jane — looping back with a concrete bridge for your counsel: we've proposed the greater-of floor at $250k with a multiple of 12x average monthly fees (previous 12 months). For the data breach carveout, our standard is $1M — Karthik noted we can increase to $1.5M with evidence of cyber insurance (we can accept Nimbus's certificate).

Key trade lines we offered:
- If Nimbus requires a $500k floor, Redwood asks for either (i) a 60-day payment term on the order form to align cash flow, or (ii) an explicit commitment to a quarterly security review and a certificate of insurance at $5M.

Would you prefer we open a quick call tomorrow to resolve? If you agree in principle, we'll push an updated MSA redline and a summarized memo of trade-offs.

Thanks,
Olga
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Jane Morris <jane.morris@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-12-09T10:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — liability cap and exclusions

Olga, Karthik — appreciate the quick turnaround and the trade options. After internal review, Nimbus will accept Redwood's proposed bridge:

• Liability cap: greater of USD 300,000 or twelve (12) times the average monthly fees paid in the prior 12 months (aggregate for the term).
• Data breach carveout: USD 1,250,000 (Nimbus will provide proof of cyber insurance at $3M).
• Consequential damages excluded (standard carveouts for IP indemnity and willful misconduct remain).

We've attached a clean redline that incorporates the agreed numbers. Please confirm and we'll route the revised MSA through DocuSign.

Best,
Jane Morris
Head of Legal, Nimbus Analytics
